summary: Internal refactor: CAD, the sketch solver bridge, the kernel bridge, CAM, the output audit, DXF and G-code imports and simulation now read every tolerance from one named precision policy in src/domain/precision/cadPrecision.ts. The policy names each tolerance by its role, states its unit and meaning, and exports CAD_PRECISION_VERSION = 1. Places that used the same value for different reasons get separate roles: kernel confusion, the smallest model length, the CAD to CAM endpoint, simulation clearance and machine geometry are all 1e-7 and stay separate. Size-based tolerances become policy functions: cadRoundoff for ulps of a magnitude, cadClosureTolerance for analytic closure, cadSupportedLength for a length within kernel confusion and the 1e6 mm model extent, and cadOutputFitting for the output audit's allowances. Each replaces an expression of the same form and gives the same bits. The survey found 434 candidate literals in non-test source; 227 moved behind 48 roles and the policy functions (47 are read at call sites; the drag floor mirrors the Rust solver), and 207 stay, each with its reason: view and pointer space, unit factors, the 1e9 coordinate budget, product limits and defaults, help text, comments, fixtures and benchmarks. A new test checks the ordering between roles, pins this version's values, checks each policy function against the expression it replaces, and checks that the Rust solver's acceptance and drag constants agree with the policy. Two relations that ought to hold do not, and are recorded as known rather than changed: the solver accepts residuals of 1e-10 mm while structural checks hold arc endpoints to closure, 1e-12 mm at sketch scales, and closure grows past kernel confusion and the CAD to CAM endpoint above about 5.6e7 mm although sketch coordinates are accepted up to 1e9 mm. Imported STEP shape tolerances and UPID planning tolerances are still adopted as they were, and are now documented. npm run lint also runs a check that flags new negative-exponent literals and Number.EPSILON outside the policy module, with a per-file list of the literals that stay. A maintainer page, docs/maintainers/precision.md, lists the roles, the ordering and how to add a role.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files, agents or controller output. Every moved tolerance keeps its value and its comparison, so geometry, CAM plans and controller output are bit-identical. No new refusal is added, and NaN handling is unchanged: cadSupportedLength replaces only checks that already had its exact form. The worker protocol, the Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged.

checklist.schema: No CAD, sketch graph, UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. Sketch annotation placement ranges read the model extent (1e6) where they wrote 1e6, with the same values. The native protocol stays version 7. The Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3. CAD_PRECISION_VERSION is new and is not yet stored anywhere.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version, cancellation or WebMCP behaviour change. Reading a role is a property read on a frozen object, and the policy functions are the expressions they replace.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added, removed or changed. No UI control or user-visible text changes.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. The output audit's point, length and arc sweep allowances come from cadOutputFitting with the same values; UPID planning tolerances from documents are still used as before.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: Identical output: the post conformance report for robofil-100-v2 is byte-identical to the same run on a snapshot of 8c7c3b50, and the UPID conformance report differs only in the absolute file paths it names. One scratch script ran on that snapshot and on this branch. It took both repository DXF files through parse, conversion to UPID, a reviewed start and controller compensation, the execution plan (81 and 13 events) and the robofil-100-v2 post with the properties of each of its three fixtures, including the post runtime's output audit, and took the two ISO evidence programs through G-code parse, structure, contours and preview. Both reports are 485,866 bytes and identical. The sketch equation baseline (5,131 inputs), relation baseline, 0.0.757 native baseline, frozen PlaneGCS corpus, released piece snapshots, controller output and controller program suites pass unchanged. Tests touched: none; vitest.config.ts adds src/domain/precision to the pure-domain project. New: cadPrecision.test.ts, 18 tests: the version 1 values and freezing, 13 ordering relations that hold and 2 known violations that must stay violated, each policy function against the expression it replaces, and agreement with the Rust solver's ACCEPT_MM, ACCEPT_RADIANS, closure ulps and drag reached floor. Swapping two roles fails an ordering relation each time: handoff endpoint and coincidence, closure floor and solver residual, approximation chord and tessellation, angular accuracy and kernel direction. Multiplying each role by 10 in turn, against the existing tests related to its readers with the new test excluded, 17 of the 47 roles read at call sites fail at least one test: minimum length 30, kernel confusion 26, CAM default coincidence 14, model extent 12, closure floor 8, solver residual 7, CAM rank relative 6, pocket cap margin 4, angular accuracy 3, frame orthonormal residual 3, closure ulps 2, DXF CAM coincidence 2, and sweep topology, tessellation angle, CAM closing duplicate, approximation chord and simulation contact 1 each. No existing test catches the other 30, which are coverage gaps: the angular roundoff cap, relative zero, the parallel cross floor, pointer minimum size, minimum angle, kernel minimum volume, kernel bounds slack, kernel direction, tessellation, the three gear roles, the CAD handoff endpoint and coincidence, the CAM default endpoint, CAM degenerate area, CAM tie, CAM rank absolute, zero length, path inside slack, the UPID recorded value floor, the output rounding guard, DXF planar normal and Z, the three G-code roles, and simulation degenerate area, obstruction and machine geometry. The drag floor has no TypeScript reader and only the Rust agreement test covers it. Related tests are found through imports, and no e2e spec ran under the mutations. Checks: full Vitest, 574 files and 6,756 tests passed (573 and 6,738 at 8c7c3b50); npm run build passed, including tsc -b with the e2e project and docs:check; npm run lint passed with zero oxlint findings and the precision literal check over 595 files, which fails as expected on probe literals; ui:check, check-release, post:conformance, upid:conformance, post:docs:check and machine-package:validate passed; check-release against origin/main fails only on the expected version gap (main 0.0.788, this record follows 0.0.790). e2e specs, each alone against the built app with 2 workers: dxf-import-units 3/3, gcode-inspection 2/2, machine-package-install 2/2, cad-workflow 32/32, cad-sketch-constraints 28/28. The Rust solver and WebAssembly module are unchanged, so solver:check was not needed. There is no machine verification.
